operators.notes: Iterate shared part hash table, collect partkeys where p_name starts with 'forest' into bitset(2000001)
Tiny table (25 rows), not shared. Scan and extract nationkey=3 for CANADA. Single scalar value.
Iterate shared supplier hash table, filter by nationkey=3. Build two structures: (1) bitset(100001) of qualifying suppkeys, (2) hash_map suppkey -> {s_name, s_address} for final projection.

operators.predicate: ps_partkey IN forest_partkeys_bitset AND ps_suppkey IN canada_suppliers_bitset
operators.notes: Filter shared partsupp scan by both bitsets. Collect (ps_partkey, ps_suppkey, ps_availqty) triples into a flat vector. Also collect distinct partkeys into a vector for index-driven lineitem lookup.
Build hash_map<(ps_partkey, ps_suppkey), ps_availqty> from the ~3494 qualifying partsupp rows. Also build a compact sorted vector of distinct partkeys (~3000) for index-driven lineitem access.

operators.filter: l_shipdate >= 8766 AND l_shipdate < 9131 AND (l_partkey, l_suppkey) IN ps_pair_hash
operators.notes: For each distinct partkey in qualifying_partsupp, use lineitem_partkey_grouped index to retrieve all lineitem row_ids for that partkey (~30 each). Filter by date range [1994-01-01, 1995-01-01) AND suppkey in canada_bitset, then aggregate SUM(l_quantity) per (partkey, suppkey). This avoids scanning 60M lineitem rows; only ~90K rows accessed via index.

For each (partkey, suppkey) pair in ps_pair_hash, look up the aggregated sum from lineitem_qty_agg. If no matching lineitem rows exist, the sum is 0 and the pair qualifies (availqty > 0). Collect distinct qualifying suppkeys into a hash_set.
Probe canada_suppliers hash_map with qualifying_suppkeys hash_set to collect (s_name, s_address) for output.
Sort ~460 result rows by s_name ascending. Trivial sort on small result set.

filters.predicate: ps_partkey IN forest AND ps_suppkey IN canada

indexes.notes: Avoids 60M-row lineitem scan. Retrieves ~30 row_ids per partkey for ~3K partkeys = ~90K total row accesses. Read l_suppkey, l_shipdate, l_quantity columns at gathered row positions.

steps_1_3.notes: Small data volumes (2M part entries, 100K supplier entries). Single-thread avoids sync overhead.

step_4.notes: 8M rows scanned but only two bitset lookups per row. Memory-bound, single thread saturates.

step_6.notes: Partition ~3K distinct partkeys across 8 threads. Each thread maintains thread-local aggregation map. Moderate parallelism due to random I/O from index lookups on HDD—too many threads would cause disk thrashing. Merge thread-local maps after.

steps_7_9.notes: ~3.5K comparisons and ~460 result rows. Trivial single-threaded work.

Two O(1) bitset lookups per partsupp row for highly selective double filter
Use lineitem_partkey_grouped index to avoid full 60M-row scan. Aggregate SUM(l_quantity) per pair.
Final semi-join to collect output columns

aggregation.notes: Small aggregation map (~3.5K entries), built during index-driven lineitem access

notes: Key optimization: index-driven lineitem access via lineitem_partkey_grouped avoids scanning 60M rows. Only ~90K row accesses needed. The correlated subquery is decorrelated into a single pass: build (partkey,suppkey)->availqty from filtered partsupp, then for each pair's partkey, use the grouped_fk index to gather lineitem rows, filter by date+suppkey, and aggregate. Compare thresholds in a final pass. Total memory: ~250KB for bitsets + ~500KB for hash maps = trivial.
